title: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) for maintenance treatment following sucessful electro-convulsive therapy (ECT) Treatment in treatment-resistant major depression
summary:
Treatment-resistant unipolar depression represents a particularly severe form of depressive disorders and is associated with a substantial individual, social, and health-economic burden. For this patient population, electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is considered one of the most effective treatment options and is recommended in current national clinical guidelines for both acute treatment and continuation/maintenance therapy. Despite successful acute treatment, the risk of relapse remains high, particularly within the first six months following remission. Maintenance ECT is an evidence-based gold-standard strategy in this context and has been shown to be superior to pharmacotherapy alone in relapse prevention.

However, the implementation of guideline-concordant maintenance ECT in routine clinical care is frequently limited. Repeated general anesthesia, high demands on personnel and infrastructure, and restricted outpatient capacity result in only a subset of patients having access to this treatment modality. This care gap is also present at the District Hospital Augsburg, where a large number of patients are successfully treated with ECT each year, but maintenance ECT can only be offered to a small proportion of remitted patients due to capacity constraints.

Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), as a non-invasive neurostimulation technique, represents a safe and established alternative. Its efficacy and safety in the treatment of acute depressive episodes are well supported by numerous studies and clinical guidelines. However, evidence regarding its use as a maintenance treatment following successful ECT is currently limited to case series and naturalistic studies, while prospective data from routine clinical settings are largely lacking.

Against this background, the present single-center MAINTAIN study prospectively investigates the feasibility and potential clinical effectiveness of a structured rTMS-based maintenance protocol following successful acute ECT in patients with treatment-resistant unipolar depression. The primary objective is to examine whether an rTMS-based maintenance strategy is associated with lower relapse rates compared to standard continuation treatment without neurostimulation.

In addition, a small naturalistic comparison group of patients receiving maintenance ECT will be observed in order to reflect local treatment practice and approximate the magnitude of effects associated with the current gold standard. The study is not designed to provide definitive evidence of efficacy but rather to generate data on feasibility, recruitment, adherence, practical implementation, relapse rates, and effect sizes as a basis for a subsequent multicenter randomized controlled trial.

In the long term, an effective and ambulatory rTMS-based maintenance strategy could help address existing treatment gaps, improve patient acceptance, and substantially reduce resource utilization compared to maintenance ECT.
conditions: Severe depression (MDD) with an indication for electroconvulsive therapy (ECT)

interventions.name:
Following completion of the acute ECT course, rTMS treatment will be initiated within 14 days. During the first treatment session, the individual resting motor threshold (RMT) will be determined to establish the stimulation intensity.

Subsequently, participants will receive weekday rTMS treatment

Treatment will be administered according to the maintenance ECT protocol routinely employed at the Department of Psychiatry and in accordance with current guideline recommendations. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnosis of treatment-resistant unipolar depression according to ICD-10 criteria
Successful completion of an acute ECT course (defined as MADRS ≤ 10)
Last ECT session no more than 14 days prior to study inclusion
Capacity to consent and provision of written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of capacity to consent
Acute suicidality (MADRS item 10 > 4) at the time of inclusion
Deep brain stimulation, vagus nerve stimulation, or other intracranial implants
Pregnancy
Documented non-response to rTMS in a previous treatment attempt (arm 1 only)
